subject: Pocket Update — Priorities, Blockers, and QBR Deliverables (June 25)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-25T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Pocket Update — Priorities, Blockers, and QBR Deliverables (June 25)

Morning all — short pocket update ahead of tomorrow's QBR dry run. I kept this tight so we can land owners and EOD actions. Please read and reply with the single-line confirmations below.

Wins (quick):
- Hosted API latency SLOs stable after the June rollout; p95 improved from 210ms -> 185ms for default model paths.
- Customer X trial (redwood-dash) moved to production validation; initial cost curves look favorable.

Risks / Tactical flags:
- Dedicated capacity forecast shows a potential shortage for the end-of-quarter burst window (week of Jul 12) unless we enable one extra reserved slot in us-west. Estimated impact: 12% increase in queuing for non-priority jobs. Owner: Jonas (see note).
- A small but visible quality regression in embeddings for long docs after quantization QA. Root cause tracked to tokenizer handling in v2 quant build. Owner: Laura.

Asks (what I need by EOD):
1) Laura — add a one-slide note with top 2 regression examples + mitigation timeline. Attach as PPTX to this thread.
2) Jonas — confirm capacity mitigation (enable +1 reserved slot or propose alternate routing) and update the capacity forecast sheet.
3) Vanessa — finalize QBR customer highlight notes (2 bullets max) and confirm if we surface the ACME cost-savings table.

Attachments: QBR-ready_list.xlsx (sheet: priorities + owner column).

Next steps: If I don't hear back by 17:00 PT, I'll assume owners are aligned and will fold these into the dry-run deck.

Thanks —
Karthik
SVP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Karthik — received. Will take the embeddings regression. Short plan:
- Deliverable: 1 slide with two concrete examples (before/after) and the short-term rollback plan.
- ETA: Draft by 15:30 PT today; final slide by 17:30 PT after QA sign-off.
- Note: Tokenizer fix will require a quick retrain on the quant build; that work is scoped and should be done by Jul 2.

Attaching qbr_sla_slide_v2.pptx (first draft) — placeholder for the regression slide; will replace with final by EOD.

On the question of customer highlights, I recommend we call out Customer X (prod validation) and the ACME cost-savings as Vanessa suggested — both are concise, measurable wins.

Thanks,
Laura

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-25T13:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pocket Update — Priorities, Blockers, and QBR Deliverables (June 25)

Plan for capacity: I ran the forecast with current commitments — options below.
- Option A (preferred): enable +1 reserved slot in us-west for Jul 10-20. Impact: ~8% increase in monthly committed spend, removes the projected burst queuing.
- Option B: activate routing policy to shift low-priority batch traffic to eu-central during the burst window. Impact: slight latency variance for batch jobs, no additional spend.

I prefer Option A to keep customer-facing latency consistent for hosted customers. I'll update the attached QBR-ready_list.xlsx (capacity tab) and mark the owner column. ETA: 16:00 PT.

Quick flag: enabling A requires written ops approval from infra finance for the commit increase — if we want to avoid procurement delays, recommend we surface this as a small QBR ask.

Jonas
Head of Prod Infra
